import html from typing import Final # Example predefined template. In real use, this would be provided elsewhere. BLOG_FORMAT: Final[str] = """

{title}

{body}
""" def publish_blog_article(subject: str, description: str) -> str: """ Sanitize and format a blog post for safe HTML display. Parameters ---------- subject : str The heading of the blog post. description : str The main text content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A string containing the sanitized and formatted blog post, ready for safe display in a browser. Raises ------ ValueError If either `subject` or `description` is empty. """ if not subject.strip(): raise ValueError("Subject cannot be empty.") if not description.strip(): raise ValueError("Description cannot be empty.") # Escape HTML special characters to prevent XSS safe_title = html.escape(subject, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(description, quote=True) # Optionally, remove any remaining script tags or inline event handlers # (simple regex approach – for more robust sanitization, use a library) import re safe_body = re.sub(r'<\s*script[^>]*>(.*?)<\s*/\s*script\s*>', '', safe_body, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL) # Format using the predefined template formatted = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body) return formatted.strip()
